---
title: "Resources: Reviewing a validation package"
order: 35
---

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 11.10 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the full "Controls for closed systems" section this module draws three clauses from: the
  introductory sentence (the obligation sits on "persons who use" a system, not its vendor),
  paragraph (a) (validation for "accuracy, reliability, consistent intended performance"), and
  paragraph (k)(2) (time-sequenced systems documentation, named as a concept only). Local
  verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/11.10.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the government's own dated, authenticated CFR collection. Use this when you need a citation
  tied to a specific published edition, not just the current rolling text Cornell's LII shows.

- **[AABB Quality Systems Framework (2021, public discussion draft PDF)](https://www.aabb.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/standards/aabb-quality-systems-framework-2021.pdf?sfvrsn=a11081d1_2)**
  — AABB's own public description of the ten Quality System Essentials, including QSE 3
  (Equipment, which explicitly covers IT systems and their qualification) and QSE 5 (Process
  Control, which covers validation). Use it to see the theme and scope of each QSE in AABB's own
  words; don't cite a standard number from it — see `sources/aabb/qse-framework.md` for why.

- **[AABB: Updated Quality Systems Essentials](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/about-aabb-standards/updated-quality-systems-essentials)**
  — AABB's current landing page on the QSE structure. Use it as a starting point for confirming
  which edition's chapter titles and numbering are currently in force before citing one precisely
  in a real Lakeshore document; see `sources/aabb/qse-framework.md`'s verification notes for what's
  still unconfirmed.

- **[FDA: Blood Establishment Computer System Validation in the User's Facility (guidance page)](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/blood-establishment-computer-system-validation-users-facility)**
  — CBER's own guidance, written for exactly Lakeshore's position: the facility using a
  commercial BECS, not the vendor. It is guidance ("should"), not regulation. Read it before
  your next package review to see FDA's recommended validation documentation in its own words.
  Local excerpt: `sources/fda-guidance/becs-validation-users-facility-2013.md`. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: General Principles of Software Validation (guidance page)](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/general-principles-software-validation)**
  — FDA's long-standing explanation of software validation: requirements, testing, and how
  evidence ties back to intended use. Written for device-software contexts, so use it for the
  reasoning behind a test plan, not as a Lakeshore-specific rule. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality Management System Software (PDF)](https://www.fda.gov/media/188844/download)**
  — the risk-based "assurance" approach to showing a system is fit for intended use. Read its
  scope section first: it addresses device manufacturers' production and quality software and
  expressly excludes device software functions, so it does not govern a blood establishment's
  validation of BECS. Useful here as a window into how FDA thinks about right-sizing test
  effort. Local excerpt: `sources/fda-guidance/csa-production-qms-software-2026-excerpt.md`.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide, 2nd Edition (publisher page)](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)**
  — the industry body's page for the risk-based computerized-system lifecycle guide behind most
  IQ/OQ/PQ vocabulary. The guide itself is a paid publication; this page is for knowing what it
  is and what edition exists, ahead of `csv-and-becs`. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[European Commission: EudraLex Volume 4, Annex 11 — Computerised Systems (PDF)](https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2016-11/annex11_01-2011_en_0.pdf)**
  — a short, readable regulator document on validation, including how a validation package
  should show a system was tested and under what controls. It is EU medicines GMP, not a US
  blood-establishment requirement; read it as a well-written comparison, not as citable
  authority for Lakeshore. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[AABB: Standards for Blood Banks and Transfusion Services](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/blood-banks-and-transfusion-services)**
  — the accreditation-side counterpart to the FDA sources above. AABB's Standards have a section
  numbered 3.9, Information Systems, which addresses the same ground this module reviews (the
  themes only; the Standards text is copyrighted and is not reproduced here). See
  `sources/aabb/information-systems-section-3.9.md` for what was and wasn't verified. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[GMP Detox IQ OQ PQ and ISPE GAMP 5 SE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gIlM-JzkoQ0)**
  (GMP Detox, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A GxP training
  channel on IQ/OQ/PQ in the context of ISPE's GAMP 5 Second Edition: the qualification structure a
  package like VIA-0842 is organized around. Training content, not a regulator or standards body,
  and about how qualification is structured rather than how to review it. Verified embeddable via
  YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
